assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity pharmacology (PROTACs and molecular glue degraders) is a new chemical modality that redirects the ubiquitin-proteasome system with small molecules, rich in mechanistic chemistry (ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design) and with clinical candidates in trials. It brings together structural, physical-organic and medicinal chemistry in a way that appeals to a molecular-level view of ligand binding.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept and first proof-of-principle compounds; Ciulli made the VHL-ligand and ternary-complex structural work that turned it into a general, drug-like platform. Handa/Ito (thalidomide-cereblon) and Gray are strong alternatives whose roles could also claim a seat; the three-person limit forces a hard choice that I regard as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Concept dates to about 2001, optimized degraders from about 2015; many degraders are in clinical trials but approval is still pending. Timely but arguably slightly early; the thalidomide mechanism work is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the PROTAC pioneers or the thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue discoverers should share the prize
Absence of an approved degrader drug as of my knowledge
I have not independently verified the clinical trial status

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is one of the most widely used bond-forming reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, built on mechanistic insight and systematic ligand design. Clear, original and of lasting practical impact, though it sits in the shadow of the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general catalytic amination with designed ligands and mechanistic studies; Kosugi/Migita's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor, but the general method is credited to the two.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of confirmation and ubiquitous use; fully mature and overdue by timing, but the 2010 prize may reduce appetite for a closely related reaction.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 Nobel Prize for cross-coupling
Credit for the early precursor work by Migita/Kosugi

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Car-Parrinello method made ab initio molecular dynamics practical by unifying electronic structure and nuclear dynamics, permitting simulation of bond breaking, liquids, solids and reactions without empirical force fields. Its influence on computational chemistry, materials and biochemistry (QM/MM style approaches) is deep and long-lasting.
assessment.attribution: Clean two-person attribution: the 1985 paper by Car and Parrinello is the single decisive contribution. Parrinello's later work (metadynamics, machine-learned potentials) is separate and need not enter the citation.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and extensive independent validation; recognition is overdue rather than premature. Computational chemistry was honored in 2013 and 2024, which might weigh against another computational prize soon.
uncertainties: Possible committee reluctance to recognize computational chemistry again after 2013 and 2024
Whether DFT-related credit (Kohn, 1998) overlaps in the committee's view

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing is a chemically designed enzyme fusion that converts one base to another without double-strand breaks, with direct therapeutic impact (first clinical applications). It is chemistry of nucleobase deamination engineered into a programmable protein, with rapid and enormous impact.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the clear intellectual leader; Komor was the lead author of the first cytosine base editor. Gaudelli led adenine base editing. Nishida/Kondo's independent cytidine-deaminase work complicates credit. A one- or two-person citation is most defensible.
assessment.maturity: Introduced in 2016, with a first clinical success in 2020s; confirmation is strong and broad, but the field is young and the 2020 CRISPR prize may be seen as overlapping.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 prize for genome editing
Allocation among Komor, Gaudelli and the Nishida/Kondo group
Long-term clinical safety evidence is limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing transformed biology and medicine by making genomes cheap to read, resting on chemistry of reversible terminator nucleotides and clonal amplification on surfaces. Impact is enormous and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry behind Solexa/Illumina; Rothberg led the pyrosequencing-based 454 platform; Mayer and Ju contributed earlier or parallel concepts. Credit is contested among several parties and a clean three-person split is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with two decades of use; recognition is timely or overdue. The 1980 prize for DNA sequencing and the competing technologies complicate scope.
uncertainties: Contested credit among platform developers and the chemistry inventors
Whether the Nobel committee sees it as chemistry versus biotechnology
Patent-driven disputes may obscure who contributed what

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite photovoltaics rose from a few percent to above 25 percent efficiency in little more than a decade, a remarkable materials-chemistry story with wide interest in energy conversion. Originality: the use of perovskite absorbers and the solid-state device architecture.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported perovskite sensitization in 2009; Park and Snaith (and Grätzel/Seok) then established the solid-state, high-efficiency devices; Kanatzidis made related lead-free materials. The three-person limit makes credit difficult and a fair configuration is unclear.
assessment.maturity: Rapid progress, but stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability remain unresolved; recognition may be premature compared with mature candidates.
uncertainties: Operational stability and lead content not yet resolved
Disagreement over who among Miyasaka, Snaith, Park, Seok and Grätzel made the decisive contribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave a physical-chemistry framework for protein folding, binding and function that underlies modern simulation and structure prediction. I regard it as conceptually fundamental for biomolecular theory, although the 2024 prize addressed prediction and design.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic with Bryngelson developed the funnel theory; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model framework; Fersht provided experimental phi-value analysis. Choosing three from these five is genuinely contested and rests on judgment rather than record.
assessment.maturity: Decades of theoretical and experimental support, though the landscape is a conceptual framework rather than a single testable discovery; timing is reasonable after the 2024 prize.
uncertainties: Whether theory and experiment (Fersht) should be recognized together
Possible perception that the 2024 prize already covered protein folding

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell has changed how cell compartmentalization is understood and links to physical chemistry of polymers and disease; the impact on biology and chemistry is large.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated P granules as liquid droplets in 2009; Rosen showed multivalent-interaction phase separation in vitro; Pappu and Mittag provide the physical-chemical theory. A three-person prize is plausible but some credit would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Still a young and debated field; the physiological relevance of many condensates is being contested and some experimental artifacts are under scrutiny. Potentially premature.
uncertainties: Debate about physiological relevance of condensates in vivo
Whether the discovery falls under chemistry rather than physiology or medicine
Allocation of theory credit (Pappu, Mittag)
